note: A list whose members are only known at runtime (issue #25). 2026-11-13: tried, not only read. A program declared with argenv 0.3.2 cannot take a repeated option with free values, nor more positionals than it names: a list needs a closed set of tokens, and only a list repeats. It is one need with three faces - snapall's --only declared as plain text (October, where this issue came from); an id typed from memory and refused three times in ocoeco's form (this week); and ocoeco's own --gathers, move TABLE ID..., and note --set, which cannot be declared at all. The three options in the issue ask how to permit free values; what the week showed is that the question is where values come from: declared (a closed set), asked (known only at runtime, and the program can tell them), or free (anything). 2026-11-13: designed (decision 2026-11-13-where-a-value-comes-from), prior art recorded (research where-values-come-from). When it lands, snapall's and lab-agent's own completion generators and oco-agent's hand-typed usage retire, and snapall's pinned test turns over: --only becomes a list whose members are asked. 2026-11-13, later the same day: the step designed here is held, not built. Seen from OCO's place (open-commons-observatory/ecosystem, decision 2026-11-13-a-command-line-is-an-entry): what argenv declares is what a lens already declares, and asked is a relation. 2026-11-13, the trial in ocoeco: argenv's reader read a lens entry against records made as the program ran - nothing here had to change. What it showed lacking is not a field: the reader looks one way, taking words in; from a blank, what may enter is not yet answered anywhere but in ocoeco's form, and it needs what only the data knows - which rows exist. 2026-11-14: the trial this waited on has run. Where a value comes from is read off the language and the rows that exist - what fits here, in ocoeco - with nothing in argenv changed (open-commons-observatory/ecosystem, decision 2026-11-13-a-command-line-is-an-entry; open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-14-what-fits-here). What is still so here: a program declared with argenv cannot take a repeated option with free values, nor a list of positionals - that is argenv's own, and no longer waits.
title: Where a value comes from - looked at as one with ocoeco's entries and relations (open question 25)

note: Found 2026-11-17 by linux-phone-oco/docs (research bringup-home-follow-and-rhizoid, decision 2026-11-17-bringup-in-lab-tools). A device repository uses lab-tools' bringup as a pinned binary or cargo git dependency; when it must patch the tool itself before upstream takes the change, the true case is a cutting of lab-tools (tracking branch pristine, patch branch merged from it, clean patch back). What rhizoid lacks is the consumption side for it: the follower declares this tool, this cutting, this tag, and rhizoid writes the pin where the language manager reads it (Cargo.toml git tag or [patch] entry; a rust-script file's cargo header; a version line in a manifest) and bumps it when the tracking branch has a new release - the open item design-consumption-side, for a case that now has a user. Until then: a plain fork and a [patch] line by hand, recorded as a problem. What is left, written 2026-11-23 (git-rhizoid-builder) against v0.3.1: the pin itself is a bump [[tool]] key - the Cargo git tag (value = "PREFIX{version}SUFFIX"), or the tag in a [patch."https://github.com/OWNER/REPO"] entry (quoted key parts, built in PR #33); the gate is cargo check and also = [Cargo.lock] (v0.2.4); a rust-script header or a manifest version line is a [[tool]] line. Left to decide: where a cutting's own releases come from, the tags bump moves a pin to. Proposed: (1) rhizoid update ... now, for a one-branch cutting whose tracking moved to a new upstream release, merges it into the patch branch (as now) and then tags the patch tip RELEASE-cut.N (lpoco-v0.43.0-cut.1; N counts this cutting's tags on that release) and pushes the tag - outward, behind now, first use behind the author's go; (2) a [[tool]] may say tag_suffix = "-cut.N", so bump reads the newest of those tags (release first, then N) as the release to pin. Rejected so far: tags made by hand (every bump would wait on a person tagging the fork); the upstream's own tag names on the fork (they would collide with the upstream's tags the fork carries); a branch pin in Cargo (cargo git branch pins move under the follower without a bump and cannot be reproduced). Done 2026-11-23: rhizoid v0.3.2 (git-rhizoid/rhizoid PR #35 with PR #33, release PR #34), as the coordinator agreed: a one-branch cutting may say cut_tags = "PREFIX"; update ... now tags the patch tip RELEASE-cut.N and pushes the tag (outward, behind now, first use per module behind the author's go), only when the patch tip differs from the newest cut tag's commit; a [[tool]] says tag_suffix = "-cut.N" and bump pins the newest cut, never a plain upstream tag the fork carries; cuts ordered by release then N, never semver (said in the README); the upstream's releases and the fork's cuts are read in rhizoid's own refs (refs/rhizoid/...), so the clone's tags are never written. A programmer review's five points fixed.
title: A cutting consumed by a language manager: the patched fork of a Rust tool as a cargo git dependency at a pinned tag, written and bumped by rhizoid

note: Named by the milestone rhizoid-carries-ocoeco's criteria but never recorded: found 2026-11-12 when ocoeco check followed every link. The milestone is right to depend on it. Design 2026-11-23 (git-rhizoid-builder, for the rhizoid lane coordinator; building waits for its read, the first real fork for the author's go): rhizcut is rhizoid's reserved verbs add, import, update, refresh and remove, built on concepts rhizoid-cutting, tracking-vs-patch-branch, clean-patch-back, fork-destination-manifest, module-metadata-file and auth-via-gh. (1) GitHub only behind GitHubPort (fork, merge_upstream, repo_exists, plus default_branch and open_pr when needed): one adapter, GhCli, drives gh (gh repo fork --org ORG --clone=false; gh api -X POST repos/FORK/merge-upstream -f branch=B; gh repo view --json), never a token of rhizoid's own; the core is tested with a fake port, the CLI with a fake gh on PATH and local bare repositories - no test touches GitHub. (2) A cutting has two branches: tracking (the upstream's branch, named in the manifest, default its default branch) moved only by merge-upstream, fast-forward, never committed to by hand; patch (rhizoid/patch, or the manifest's name) where every change lives, merged from tracking. .rhizoid/module.toml (origin, tracked_ref, last_synced_commit, added_as, attached_on) lives on the patch branch only, so tracking stays fast-forwardable and diff tracking...patch minus .rhizoid/ is the clean patch back. (3) Verbs, each listing what it would do and changing nothing unless given now (practice 8): add SOURCE now forks SOURCE into the org (manifest default or --org), makes the patch branch with module.toml from tracking, pushes it, records [[module]] in rhizoid.toml; import FORK now adopts an existing fork the same way (its upstream read from GitHub's parent); update [MODULE] now runs merge-upstream on tracking, then merges tracking into patch in a fresh worktree (a conflict stops it, names the paths, keeps nothing) and pushes; refresh [MODULE] reads what each fork is and says where the manifest and the forks differ, changing nothing; remove MODULE drops the manifest entry and never deletes a fork (deleting a GitHub repository stays a person's act). (4) Every outward step - a fork created, a branch pushed, merge-upstream - is printed before it is taken and only with now; the first real add waits for the author's go through the coordinator. (5) What follows rhizcut, not in it: status's fork-track already reads tracking against upstream; send-back of the clean patch as an upstream pull request reuses send-back; consuming a cutting as a cargo dependency is cutting-as-cargo-dependency (rank 9), whose pin is a bump [[tool]] key. Rejected: rhizoid's own GitHub token or API client (auth-via-gh: no credentials to keep); module.toml on the tracking branch (merge-upstream could no longer fast-forward); deleting forks in remove (irreversible, outward); a cutting without a patch branch (changes on tracking would conflict with upstream forever). Done 2026-11-23: rhizoid v0.3.0 (git-rhizoid/rhizoid PR #29, release PR #30), with the coordinator's three changes: the graph is the record (decision 2026-11-23-cuttings-live-in-the-graph; rhizoid.toml and init retired); patches = integration for a kernel's topics (no patch branch, nothing pushed); every GitHub-writing verb's first real use per module waits for the author's go through the coordinator. A programmer review's seven points fixed: the fork is the clone's remote by URL (the real sxmo-utils clone's origin is its upstream), merge-upstream checked to be a fast-forward first, add finishes in one run, a failed push's branch adopted, record conflicts block the plan, the graph edit keeps CRLF, quotes and comments. Tests use a fake gh and local bare repositories only.
title: rhizcut: the tool that takes a cutting

note: Found 2026-11-17 by linux-phone-oco/docs (same research). clean-patch-back says a diff of the patch branch against the pristine tracking branch is a clean patch; the CLI that makes it and opens the pull request is stubbed. The follower's bases keep an upstream item per change (idealkb: ikb upstream-item, form patch, draft, ready on the person's word, sent with the PR address, landed when released). Lacking: a rhizoid verb that, for a changed generic file or a patch branch, writes the patch, opens the pull request only after the person says ready, and returns the PR address and later the release that carried it, in a form the follower's record command takes - without rhizoid knowing that base's tables. It never sends in the person's name by itself. Reshaped 2026-11-18 (docs research base-graph-measured, base-graph-world; decision 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs; upstream item rhizoid-scope-every-edge (linux-phone-oco/docs)): rhizoid's scope is the follow tool for every edge (slice, tool pin, cutting), built in order status-over-every-edge, follow-by-conformance, send-back, cuttings; each replaces shell only once it passes the shell's tests. Unparking implement-cli waits on the author's word. Reshaped 2026-11-23 (decisions 2026-11-23-rhizoid-carries-the-structure-git-flows, 2026-11-23-structure-flows-ranked-first; linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-git-flows-run-on-rhizoid): rebase topic/ITEM onto the target tree onto send/ITEM/vN (stop naming the commit at a conflict); format-patch --cover-letter -vN --base into the folder given (upstream/LIST/ITEM/vN-draft/); range-diff vs topic/ITEM/vN-1; a changelog skeleton from it; --base and the tested commit (passed in, never guessed) for SEND-NOTES; get_maintainer.pl recipients; checkpatch --strict stops it (a missing SoB and an unresolvable Fixes listed, not hidden); W=1 / dt-check as a check command by exit code. Out: signing, re-authoring, send-email, pushing, lore, b4, claims in the cover letter. Record fields, settled by ikb 2026-11-23 (relayed by the Top Coordinator): send-back prints exactly ikb upstream-item's option names as key=value - version=vN, carried-in=FORK/topic/ITEM (FORK the fork's upstreams id, from the graph), local-ref=topic/ITEM/vN, file=upstream/DEST/ITEM/ (it must start with upstream/); never sent-on or forwarded. Base, base_sha and the tested commit are printed as they are; the caller puts them in the item's note. Done 2026-11-23: rhizoid v0.2.1 (git-rhizoid/rhizoid PR #15, release PR #16), general under decision 2026-11-23-rhizoid-stays-general. rhizoid send-back BRANCH --onto REF --out DIR [--config FILE] [--tested SHA] [--fork ID]: rebase onto the target in a fresh worktree (authorship kept, nothing signed, no other branch moved; a conflict names the commit and keeps nothing); format-patch --cover-letter -vN --base into --out with --range-diff against the previous version's tag and a changelog skeleton; the checks and the recipients command are argv in rhizoid's config [send] (the Linux kernel's checkpatch --strict, W=1, dt_binding_check and get_maintainer.pl are examples/kernel-send.toml; exceptions are the check's own arguments); SEND-NOTES with the base, the tested commit and every check's output; the version tag and send branch made only when every check passes. Prints ikb's keys version, carried-in, local-ref, file. Out: signing, re-authoring, send-email, pushing, lore, b4, claims in the cover letter. Reshaped in v0.2.2 (2026-11-23, PR #19), after the recorded flow (docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-kernel-topics-and-integration: topic/ITEM/vN is the author's signed, sent tip) and the upstreams lane: send-back makes drafts - numbered one past the versions sent ({branch}/v{n}, tagged by the author: the one manual step, git tag topic/ITEM/vN <signed tip>), tagged {branch}/v{n}-draft; a re-run for the same N is cut beside the earlier draft and replaces it only when ready (replaced=yes), never a branch, tag or folder that is not this draft's; range-diff against the version last sent; a shallow history that cannot hold the base or the version last sent is refused before writing; local-ref is the branch, draft=vN and draft_tag replace version=; a step with fails = false is reported only (the draft's expected checkpatch findings, as data in examples/kernel-send.toml); the cover letter's testing line is a marked blank.
title: Sending a change back: a patch to the source as a pull request, and the follower's own record of it

note: Found 2026-11-17 by grenudi/ideal-knowledge-base (research chain-follow-world, decision 2026-11-17-chain-follow-by-slice). Its chain - idealkb to device-template to device bases - lays a slice, not a repository: a source names what it gives (a generic list, files whole or the part between two marker lines), a follower pins a release and names its own files, and the verdict says whether the follower changed a generic file (idealkb's bin/follow.sh ends 3). rhizoid today takes a whole fork (a cutting); this is the consumption side design-consumption-side leaves open. follow.sh and update-pins.sh are the prototype; when rhizoid has it, idealkb can hand its chain over. Also lacking for that chain: the pin read from the follower's own file, a release gate (every follower answers before a release is tagged), and sending a changed generic file back as a patch. Also 2026-11-17: the tools home (linux-phone-oco/lab-tools) has the same slice case for the device-template files that go with a tool - the [boot] manifest skeleton, hook examples, an initramfs skeleton - beside the tool's own version pin (see cutting-as-cargo-dependency, followers-one-pin-bump). Reshaped 2026-11-18 (docs research base-graph-measured, base-graph-world; decision 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs; upstream item rhizoid-scope-every-edge (linux-phone-oco/docs)): rhizoid's scope is the follow tool for every edge (slice, tool pin, cutting), built in order status-over-every-edge, follow-by-conformance, send-back, cuttings; each replaces shell only once it passes the shell's tests. Unparking implement-cli waits on the author's word. What is left, written 2026-11-23 against what follow (rank 6) does: laying a slice and reading the pin from the follower's own file are done by rhizoid follow; (a) a slice pin moved on a branch, gated like a tool, is bump now (built here); (b) one pin file the follower owns for every kind is not built - decision 2026-11-23-pins-stay-with-their-readers; the release gate stays idealkb's followers-answer.sh (it asks idealkb's queries); sending a changed generic file back as a patch is its own row, generic-file-back.

note: Found 2026-11-18 by linux-phone-oco (docs research base-graph-measured, base-graph-world; decision 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs; upstream item rhizoid-scope-every-edge (linux-phone-oco/docs)). Edges are read from the pin files followers already own (idealkb.toml, devicebase.toml, lab.toml [tools], a fork's .rhizoid/module.toml), so the follower lists derive from the pins. Built in rhizoid-cli: status reads a graph file of the edges and each follower's own pin files at origin/main, reports every edge current, behind or moved by hand, exits 1 on drift, and is proven by graph-drift.sh's cases as fixtures and by agreeing with graph-drift.sh run on the real graph. Released 2026-11-18 as git-rhizoid/rhizoid v0.1.0 (PRs 7, 8, 9): rhizoid status over a graph file (examples/linux-phone-oco.graph.toml: slice, device layer, tool pin, fork), agreeing with graph-drift.sh edge by edge on the real graph (tests/agree-with-graph-drift.sh). Unknowns shown as not known yet. From the Steward's point 4 and walleye. It is general under decision 2026-11-23-rhizoid-stays-general: a graph's [[integration]] edge (repo, release_prefix, scheme, topics, assembled) and not a kernel edge, and the kernel layout is examples/kernel.graph.toml. Checks: name-scheme (an int/ branch is outside the kernel example's scheme: test kernels are tags only), topic-base, branch-origin (a local topic that differs from origin's), recipe (each assembled list's newest tag read back; a tag of the assembled shape without a recipe), worktree-tag (rhizoid's worktrees, locked or left unlocked at a conflict). not-known-yet is never drift. --fetch prunes branches, never tags. Fork -> upstream stays a [[fork]] edge. The same release carries the Steward's three assemble refinements (--done TAG, an unchanged list makes no tag, tested_commit a full sha) and the ikb keys (entry.N.source, one BRANCH.WITH.DOTS=sha line per entry, tested=).

note: Cause found 2026-11-09 by tracing every request the ADSP makes (a verbose hexagonrpcd build on the phone): the sensors service (hexagonrpcd -s) attaches the ADSP sensor process, whose registry init re-reads the sensor configs and needs to write (temp.json); hexagonrpcd refuses all writes, the firmware asserts (SNS_REG_INIT) and the whole ADSP restarts, taking audio with it. No registry state fixes it (packaged, or the phone own from persist, readable, with the version marker - which hexagonrpcd also never serves: a real gap, patch drafted). Fix in place on the phone: hexagonrpcd-adsp-sensorspd masked. Result: 0 ADSP crashes across three boots and many minutes, the POCO X3 sound card up at about 12 s, playback without crashes. Trade-off: no ADSP sensors, which did not work anyway. Next: propose upstream (do not start sensorspd on surya until registry writes are supported; serve sns_reg_version in hexagonrpcd); see sensors-registry-writes. Settled 2026-11-11: fixed by masking the audio processor's helper services (hexagonrpcd rootpd, sensorspd).
title: The ADSP crashes every 13-25 s, restarting audio each time

note: Trigger found 2026-11-10, one change at a time: with hexagonrpcd's RootPD helper (a FastRPC client) attached, the audio DSP dies on every suspend attempt - 24 of 24 (fatal error EX:kernel:0x0:IST46:0x132:PC=0xf0049be4, about 30 ms after the attempt; the attempts abort at once because the USB link cannot go idle). Without the helper: 0 of 8, and on a clean boot with it masked 0 of 9, all checks passing; sound does not need it. Not a first-boot effect, not the sensor proxy, no stream open. The earlier "rare" crash (2 of 28, both early in a boot) was the same one: there the helper died with the first crashes and stayed down. Fixed in the lab: hexagonrpcd-adsp-rootpd masked in the device manifest, baked in at every flash. Still open, for upstream: why an attached FastRPC client makes the DSP assert across a suspend attempt (the kernel's fastrpc and remoteproc suspend handling, or hexagonrpcd), and why the helper restarts after each crash on a fresh system. Settled 2026-11-11: fixed with the same masks and the awake service.
title: The audio DSP crashes right after resume from suspend

note:
With the sensors service off, one boot (2026-11-09) never announced the ADSP audio services, so no sound card until the ADSP was restarted by hand. Not reproduced in two further valid cold boots (audio services about 0.1-0.2 s after the ADSP, card present). Watch for it; if it recurs, check whether the in-kernel pd-mapper was loaded before the ADSP booted.

2026-11-17: no longer rare - 3 of 8 boots that night (stock and test kernels alike) came up with the ADSP running but no audio services, so no sound card; restarting remoteproc0 (stop, start) brought the card back each time. The speaker's support is only as good as this; a fix, or at least a recovery at boot, is next after the microphone - or before it if it keeps recurring.

2026-11-17, read from the phone's journal (bring-up): in a bad boot the ADSP comes up but the APR audio services (aprsvc:service:4:3/4/7/8) are never added; in a good boot they appear 0.2 s after 'remote processor adsp is now up'. In the bad boot they appeared only right after the manual ADSP restart. So the protection-domain up notification (PDR, through the in-kernel PD mapper) never arrived. qcom_pd_mapper is a module nothing depends on (lsmod: used by 0), so it can load after the ADSP has booted. Next: load qcom_pd_mapper before the remoteprocs (modules-load.d through the device manifest, or the initramfs), count bad boots over twenty reboots before and after; then the kernel fix (pas depending on the PD mapper) for upstream.

2026-11-17 trial (bring-up): with /etc/modprobe.d/devlab-pd-mapper.conf on the phone (softdep qcom_q6v5_pas pre: qcom_pd_mapper) 13 of 13 boots came up with the sound card, against 8 failing of 42 health runs before. Other distributions do the same (omarchy puts qcom_pd_mapper in the initramfs for Snapdragon laptops). Next: twenty more boots, then carry the file in device.toml's flash overlays with its reason, and the kernel-side fix (the remoteproc driver depending on the PD mapper) for upstream.

Done 2026-11-17 (bring-up): 21 of 21 boots with the sound card since the PD mapper loads before the remoteproc driver; surya's device.toml now carries lab/devlab-pd-mapper.conf to /etc/modprobe.d in every flash. The kernel-side form for upstream is backlog upstream-pd-mapper-order.
title: One cold boot came up without audio services

note:
Asked for 2026-11-10: the conveyor as a repo of its own, so anyone can bring support to another phone with the same conveyors, CI, tests, tad page and automatic integration into the grand picture; surya is the first instance, not the mould.

Design. (1) linux-phone-oco/device-template, a GitHub template repository: Use this template makes <vendor>-<codename>-lab. (2) device.toml, one manifest per device - codename, SoC, compatible strings, panel variants, image sources, how to reach the phone - read by every script; no script edited per device. (3) Generic machinery, generalized from surya-lab: the phone library (USB or Wi-Fi, commands on stdin), flashing with built-in fixes, provisioning (packages, Wi-Fi from private files), switching shells, device-tree audits, an upstream queue with send commands generated by get_maintainer.pl. (4) Tests as small independent checks, one file each declaring its component and what it needs, so a device runs the checks that apply; results as JSON lines with a versioned schema. (5) Device-independent analysis in linux-phone-oco/lab-tools (Rust): tone (speaker tests microphone) first. (6) Onboarding conveyor: a lab-tools command reads a running phone (compatible, inputs, outputs, sound devices) and fills device.toml - and from the same facts generates the Sxmo device profile. (7) Each device repo publishes its own tad data (support status, test runs, wiki claims) with CI that validates it and renders its page. (8) Integration: a feed in linux-phone-oco/docs discovers device repos by a GitHub topic and pulls their published tables, so a new device appears in the devices table and the support grid (tad draws device x component as a matrix) with no hand edits. (9) Conventions in AGENTS.md: explicit intent for state changes, lists as arguments, secrets outside repos, fingerprints before trusting images. (10) Proof: surya-lab re-based onto the template as its first instance - still 18 of 18 through it. Landscape read 2026-11-10 (see the landscape table): build on what exists - device.toml derives from postmarketOS deviceinfo; tests take the shape of pmOS's initramfs CI tests and use bootrr for driver probes; the lab aims to be a CI-tron-compatible setup and surya a device under test in pmOS's hardware farm; flashing leans on pmbootstrap. 

2026-11-17: made - linux-phone-oco/device-template (a GitHub template): a lab is device.toml, tests/health, tests/results and its records; every tool is devlab's. Proven on surya the same day: the phone checks its own health after every boot (devlab-health, a static Rust runner, generic checks in postmarketOS's test shape, [health] in the manifest, known gaps measured but not ill health), every change devlab makes ends with that report, devlab gather now files the runs here (9 runs filed, a week of filing by hand caught up), devlab mcp is the door for agents. Open: surya-lab re-based onto it, a second phone through it, device.toml read off a running phone, the Alpine package through the package conveyor.
title: A device template: the conveyor any phone's support is built on

Taken up 2026-11-17 by the bring-up session, as the weakest link the data shows: audio-mic and audio-earpiece are both broken and two milestones rest on them (surya-sound, and the calls of surya-phone and lp-calls-and-messages), while the other broken parts (cameras, fingerprint, sensors) rest only on every-part and the modem waits for a SIM card. Where it stands (surya-audio/wcd-boots, 2026-11-11): with the LPI pin-mux fix (pins 19 and 23: swr_tx_data and swr_rx_data at their right function index) the WCD9375 enumerates on both SoundWire buses, binds, and the card POCO X3 is made with the codec's controls. Capture then fails at prepare: the TX SoundWire master (62ed0000) reads nothing back from the codec (swrm_wait_for_rd_fifo_avail read underflow, reading DPN_PortCtrl of port 1, addr 0x102), so Program transport params fails with -5 - also with the bus and codec held awake. Next: a health check that records from the main microphone and fails until it hears a signal (test first), then the read-back on the TX bus: compare the TX data pins and the controller's read settings with the vendor kernel and sibling SoCs (sm6150, sm7125).

2026-11-17, night (bring-up): the check mic-records runs after every boot (a known gap until it passes). In one-off test kernels the cause narrowed: about a millisecond after the sound card registers, the WCD9375 drops off both SoundWire buses at once and is never enumerated again, so the capture's port setup gets no answer. Ruled out: the clock-stop resume path, runtime suspend, headset detection, and any traced register write, supply or GPIO in that window. Lead: our device tree's active reset pin state drives the active-low reset low, where the vendor's drives it high. Next: a try with the reset's active state output-high, logging the bus-level SoundWire writes at card registration. Full record: surya-lab research/microphone.md.

2026-11-17, later (bring-up): the drop is explained and fixed - ASoC puts idle components into their sleep pin state, and the codec's sleep state held its reset low (traced to snd_soc_bind_card). Fixed on linux-phone-oco/linux PR #4 (with the SoundWire pin-mux fix as PR #3), both queued in upstream-queue for sm7150-mainline, waiting for the author to send. With it the codec stays attached and capture prepares, but delivers exact zeros. The built-in microphones are digital mics (TX DMIC1-3); this DSP rejects the VA capture port, so they go through the TX macro. Next: why the TX decimators deliver zeros (register sequence against the vendor's tx-macro), then the DMIC route. Tests use no sound louder than the author allows (lab-tools test-sound-level-setting).

note: Plasma Mobile (fresh Nura image, sound fixes applied on the phone): speakers were silent with the whole chain playing. Two causes, both confirmed: (1) the image restores a saved mixer state with both amplifiers' digital volume at 0 = -110 dB; (2) a tas2562 driver bug: setting the Digital Volume Control changes only the driver's cache, the chips (page 2, 0x0c-0x0f) stay at -110 dB. Writing 0x40000000 straight into both chips with i2cset made sound work: the user heard YouTube in Firefox, 2026-11-10. Not persistent: after a power-off the restore and the driver bug bring the silence back. Needed: the driver fix (upstream-tas2562-volume), and until then a boot-time step that writes the volume into the chips. Root cause found and fixed 2026-11-10: the tas2562 driver's maximum volume (0 dB) read past the end of its lookup table, which muted the amps; with two more faults (the latch byte written first, resume skipping bytes). Fixed module installed and proven on the phone by I2C reads; every flash bakes it in. Listen on Plasma when it is next run.
title: Plasma Mobile: speakers silent, the chain playing

note: 2026-11-24: the lab stuck at 0.48.11 - follow's round got 'cannot fetch ...releases (HTTP 403)'. gh on the lab is logged in only through GH_TOKEN in interactive shells; the follow unit has none, so it asks api.github.com anonymously and the lab's address is rate limited. Decided (orchestration): follow takes the newest family tag from git ls-remote --tags (git over https, not the REST rate limit) and fetches each asset and its .sha256 from https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/releases/download/TAG/NAME, checking the sum; the API stays only as a fallback. Rejected: conditional requests (GitHub counts a 304 free only for authorized requests - check the doc and name it); giving the unit the lab's token (Top: it stays out of follow); a stored gh login (the author's hand, and still one token for everything). Next lead: the moment of failure is when the bus is reshaped for the stream - compare the TX controller's frame and port parameters with the phone's Android kernel. Compared with the Android kernel: the TX bus's port layout and timings match (ports 2-5 as on sm8250 mainline and the vendor), so not the port table. The first read of a port register (DP1 PortCtrl) at stream prepare fails while hundreds of codec register accesses worked at init. Next: trace the bus's transfers (dynamic debug on the SoundWire bus and the qcom controller, or a kernel with SoundWire debugfs - this one has none). note: Solved 2026-11-11: the audio pin driver muxed gpio19 (TX SoundWire data) to function 1 and gpio23 (RX data) to 3, where the phone's own Android kernel has 3 and 2. note: The commons' rule is a declared command line (argenv). ocoeco still uses clap; the entries of lenses are checked for collisions by the build script. When ocoeco moves to argenv, each entry's flags become part of the declared contract. 2026-11-13: the most valuable of the five to move. Lens entries are taken before the parser by hand, because the older library could not take what lenses declare; with argenv a build step makes the declarations from the lens files, so entries are real commands with help, completions and man pages, and a collision is the compiler's to find. 2026-11-13, looked at what argenv carries: typed inputs (text, yes or no, one of a set, a list, numbers, a path), options that repeat, positionals, inputs scoped to one command, and usage and a schema made from the one declaration. Nothing ocoeco needs is missing for the move; only offering the id of an existing row waits on argenv's own open item (a list known only at runtime). The author has set this first: the fulldome's form tells how to use it from a legend typed by hand - a program dictating its use from behind brackets. 2026-11-13, set right: it was said here that nothing ocoeco needs is missing in argenv. That was read off the names of its fields, not tried. Tried: a repeated option with free values, and more positionals than are named, cannot be declared. The need is met in argenv, where it lives, before ocoeco moves. 2026-11-13, the trial (a throwaway program, nothing changed in either repository): the item entry of the work lens, turned into records as the program runs, was read by argenv's own reader as it is. Eight typed lines: what was given was read, with the door each value came through (who is driving came from the environment - what the computer supplies and argenv's second door are one thing); a misspelt word was answered with what was meant; a value outside the set was refused with the set, taken from the lens; a missing id and a missing value were named. Three signs: needed is not one thing (a title is needed for a new row, not for a change - known only from what exists, and a record can only say always); the reader cannot say a link points nowhere (what a relation knows has nowhere to go in a record); and it reads what was typed but does not say what could be. So it no longer waits on argenv: nothing in argenv had to change. 2026-11-13: done for entries - a typed line is read back by argenv's reader (decision 2026-11-13-a-surface-reads-back); ocoeco's own reader of typed words is retired. 2026-11-13: the reader speaks for itself - what it could not take is said in argenv's own words, with only what the entry knows added (what it asks).
